Package org.checkerframework.framework.stubifier

Class BinaryStubFileGeneratorTest

java.lang.Object
org.checkerframework.framework.stubifier.BinaryStubFileGeneratorTest
public class BinaryStubFileGeneratorTest extends Object
Tests for BinaryStubFileGenerator's two modes (per-file siblings, and a whole-directory --bundle), and for the source-fingerprint staleness detection that BinaryStubData.matchesSource(byte[]) provides for a user-supplied -Astubs file (see AnnotationFileElementTypes#commandLineBinaryStub, which relies on it instead of comparing file modification times).

These tests call BinaryStubFileGenerator.main(java.lang.String[]) directly, so they exercise only its success paths: its usage-error and bundle-name-collision paths call System.exit, which would terminate the test JVM, and are intentionally not exercised here.

    directoryModeRecursesIntoNestedJar()
    A directory passed to per-file mode is searched recursively for .jar files, not just .astub files, and each one found is updated the same way a directly-named .jar root would be -- matching AnnotationFileUtil's directory walk, which likewise descends into a nested .jar when resolving -Astubs.
    void
    jarModeRemovesEntryThatNoLongerParses()
    When a .astub entry that already has a binary sibling is edited into something unparseable, regenerating removes the now-unregenerable sibling instead of leaving it behind: unlike the directory case (which calls deleteStaleOutput) or a bundle (which is rewritten from scratch each time), a JAR is modified incrementally, so this must be handled explicitly -- otherwise the stale sibling would trigger a stale.binary.stub warning on every future compilation, with the tool's own suggested fix (re-running it) unable to clear it.
    void
    jarModeReplacesStaleEntry()
    Regenerating a JAR whose entries already have binary siblings from a previous run replaces them, rather than leaving stale duplicates.
    void
    jarModeWritesEntriesInPlace()
    A .jar input root has each of its .astub entries pre-parsed into a new sibling .astub.bin.gz entry, written into the same JAR file in place: the original entries are untouched, and the output directory argument is ignored (there is nowhere else a JAR's own entries could sensibly be written).
    void
    perFileModeWritesReadableSibling()
    Per-file mode writes a sibling .astub.bin.gz whose recorded fingerprint matches the exact source bytes it was generated from, and no other bytes.

    • directoryModeRecursesIntoNestedJar

      public void directoryModeRecursesIntoNestedJar() throws Exception
      A directory passed to per-file mode is searched recursively for .jar files, not just .astub files, and each one found is updated the same way a directly-named .jar root would be -- matching AnnotationFileUtil's directory walk, which likewise descends into a nested .jar when resolving -Astubs. Without this, a nested jar's entries could never get a binary form through the enclosing directory root, permanently triggering the "incomplete binary stub setup" warning with no way to clear it.
      Throws:
      Exception

    • bareRelativeBundleRootDoesNotCrash

      public void bareRelativeBundleRootDoesNotCrash() throws Exception
      A bare relative input root with no directory component (e.g. "project-stubs", the exact form the manual's own --bundle example uses) must not crash: Path#getParent() is null for such a path, which Files.createTempFile rejects with a NullPointerException unless the path is first made absolute. BinaryStubFileGenerator.main(java.lang.String[]) resolves relative arguments against the process's current working directory, which cannot be changed within this JVM once started, so this runs the generator in a genuinely separate process with a controlled working directory, passing bare relative names exactly as a user would from within that directory.
      Throws:
      Exception
